To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the struggles in translating EA practices to users and connecting EA practices to existing norms can be overcome through the techniques of inductive communication and the deployment of local experts.

1) institutional change and translation theory can be used to understand the implementation of EA in a government context; 2) the institutionalization of EA in a US state context is a contested practice that requires inductive communication and the deployment of expert knowledge; and 3) EA implementation in a US state requires a focus on both technical and institutional aspects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the institutionalization of EA and its implications for practice.
the institutionalization of IS practices in organizations and how to overcome the institutional struggles that are encountered in this process.
how IS organizations translate new practices into existing institutional contexts, and how these practices become institutionalized.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the institutional change and translation approach is useful in understanding and explaining the struggles in the implementation of EA practices.
institutionalization of contested IS practices is a complex process that requires a combination of techniques to translate and connect new practices.
this study provides insights into the process of institutionalization of EA practices in a government setting and provides guidance on how to implement EA practices in a contested setting.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EA practice is not a technology but a set of practices that can be implemented and institutionalized in organizations.

EA implementation in government is an institutional change process that is characterized by the struggles of translation and connection, which can be overcome through the use of techniques that facilitate the process.
the EA implementation in this US state government was institutionalized by translating the new practices to connect with existing institutionalized practices and values.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the process of institutionalization is more than just getting users to accept a new practice.
the institutional change process is a complex one and that the institutionalization of contested practices requires the deployment of multiple change agents and techniques.
the institutionalization process is not a one-way process, but rather a continuous, two-way process of change and translation.
